collectionunit.notes: "At the far north end of Five Mile Beach swamp a pit was excavated in Melaleuca ericifolia heath at the centre of the valley between the second sand ridge and the granite hills, and to the west of Five Mile Creek[...] Initially samples at 20 cm intervals were treated. Further samples were selected in intervals where the complexity of pollen changes warranted more intensive study."-(Ladd,1979)
collectionunit.location: About a quarter of the way down from the top of the bounding box. Midway horizontally.

site.sitedescription: "Five Mile Beach swamp occupies an extensive embayment in the granite hills on the eastern side of Wilsons Promontory. A large expanse of swampy land has formed behind a barrier system which was probably built across the mouth of the embayment in the Pleistocene and Holocene, at times when sea level was similar to the present[…] A large part of the swamp is composed of a mat of vegetation over water and unconsolidated peat, but at the northern end the peat is solid and in summer the water table is below the surface[…]The vegetation around the Five Mile Beach swamp ranges from small areas of Nothofagus cunninghamii - Atherosperma moschatuni closed forest above 250 m on Mount Latrobe at the far south end of the catchment, to Salicornia-Juncus salt marsh at the far north end of the beach. The broad sheltered gullies to the south and west of the swamp support Eugenia smithii closed-forest, e.g. Paradise Gully[…]and Eucalyptus globulus or E. obliqua tall open-forest with an understorey of ferns, broad-leaved shrubs and Acacia melanoxylon. Most of the slopes above the swamp are covered by E. obliqua and E. baxteri open-forest, except in exposed situations such as at the northern end where heath replaces forest, probably as the result of fires in the recent past."-(Ladd,1979)
